About the Role: Crusoe's Managed AI team builds the services customers use to customize and run large language models without managing infrastructure. On the training side, it's a post-training platform where customers adapt models to their own data with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL). On the inference side, it's managed serving that runs open-weight and fine-tuned models, including LoRA adapters, fast and cost-efficiently on Crusoe's GPU fleet. The two are closely connected: models trained on the platform are deployed and served on the same infrastructure, and RL training depends on high-throughput inference for rollouts. As an AI Applied Research PhD Intern, you'll own a research question somewhere on that path from training to serving. It could be making RL work reliably on real customer tasks, or making inference faster and cheaper without losing quality. You'll run experiments on frontier open-weight models (Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek and Kimi-class models) on large GPU clusters, turn your findings into recipes and platform features that customers use, and present the results to the team and leadership. This is a 12-week, full-time, in-person internship. Candidates who want to see their research run in production, not just in a paper, will find it a good fit. What You'll Bring to the Team: Education: Currently enrolled in a PhD program in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Electrical Engineering or a related field, with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 and Spring 2029. Research experience: 2+ years of research experience in machine learning or ML systems, including hands-on work with large language models: training or fine-tuning (SFT, RLHF, DPO, GRPO/PPO) or inference optimization. Programming: Strong Python and PyTorch; comfortable reading and modifying large ML codebases. Experimental rigor: You design controlled experiments, choose the right baselines and metrics, and can tell a real effect from noise. Systems awareness: Working knowledge of how LLM training and inference run on GPUs, such as batching, memory, mixed precision and parallelism. Communication: You explain complex results clearly in writing and in person, and you work well with engineers turning research into product. Bonus Points Publications at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys, ACL, EMNLP or COLM on RL for LLMs, reward modeling, agents, efficient training or efficient inference. Hands-on experience with inference engines (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) or training frameworks (verl, OpenRLHF, TRL, Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed). Experience with quantization, speculative decoding, GPU kernels (CUDA, Triton) or LoRA/PEFT methods. Experience building agent environments, tool-use sandboxes or evaluation harnesses. Open-source contributions to Training/Infernece libraries. description: About Basis Basis is a nonprofit applied AI research organization with two mutually reinforcing goals. The first is to understand and build intelligence. This means to establish the mathematical principles of what it means to reason, to learn, to make decisions, to understand, and to explain; and to construct software that implements these principles. The second is to advance society’s ability to solve intractable problems . This means expanding the scale, complexity, and breadth of problems that we can solve today, and even more importantly, accelerating our ability to solve problems in the future. To achieve these goals, we’re building both a new technological foundation that draws inspiration from how humans reason, and a new kind of collaborative organization that puts human values first. About the Role Research interns work closely with scientists and engineers at Basis, learning from and contributing to our team. Internships are open to graduate-level candidates (or equivalent), pursuing research in technical and scientific domains, including areas of computer science such as machine learning, and programming languages. We are looking for people who want to grow technically and who value gaining a deeper understanding of concepts at their foundations. We expect you to: Have demonstrated an ability to do high-quality scientific research. Possible ways to demonstrate this include publications, technical reports, and software projects In addition, the following would be an advantage: Excited about solving real world problems and having positive societal impact Activities Develop and explore computational theories of intelligence, including reasoning, learning, and decision-making In close collaboration with domain experts inside and especially outside Basis, work as a team member to help solve scientific and societal problems Distill insights from solving problems into more general mathematical and computational theories Contribute to open-source software (Optionally) Publish and present findings in journals and conferences Contribute to the culture and direction of Basis Potential projects Interns will be placed with one of our active challenge projects or our core tech team , according to project needs and intern fit. In particular, we have openings within the following areas, but this list is not exhaustive: Dynamical Systems + Machine Learning at Basis We’re seeking interns interested in developing the theory and methods that let us learn how systems work from data—and quantify what we don’t know. This work sits at the intersection of machine learning, dynamical systems, and uncertainty quantification , with the goal of advancing how we represent, infer, and forecast complex real-world processes under uncertainty. Projects may be theoretical (developing foundations for learning and reasoning about dynamics), methodological or engineering-focused (building and integrating algorithms into our universal reasoning engine), or applied (using our existing toolkits to study systems such as animal behavior and robot co-design ). Recent blogpost: Introducing Dynestyx, a probabilistic programming library for dynamical systems Interns should have familiarity with differential equations , machine learning , and Bayesian inference . Secure Sensing & Robotics We are starting a new hardware research effort on privacy-centered hardware. The ubiquity of IoT devices and never-ending appetite of large-scale AI models have normalized mass data recording and mining of public and private spaces. This motivates numerous research questions: (1) how do we design public interest IoT and robotics applications that preserve community members’ privacy? (2) How can we design checks and balances in sensing systems to affirm compliance with consent and anti-eavesdropping laws? (3) How do we center trustworthiness in the design of IoT and robotic system? About the Role: Crusoe's Managed AI team builds the services customers use to customize and run large language models without managing infrastructure. On the training side, it's a post-training platform where customers adapt models to their own data with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL). On the inference side, it's managed serving that runs open-weight and fine-tuned models, including LoRA adapters, fast and cost-efficiently on Crusoe's GPU fleet. The two are closely connected: models trained on the platform are deployed and served on the same infrastructure, and RL training depends on high-throughput inference for rollouts. As an AI Applied Research PhD Intern, you'll own a research question somewhere on that path from training to serving. It could be making RL work reliably on real customer tasks, or making inference faster and cheaper without losing quality. You'll run experiments on frontier open-weight models (Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek and Kimi-class models) on large GPU clusters, turn your findings into recipes and platform features that customers use, and present the results to the team and leadership. This is a 12-week, full-time, in-person internship. Candidates who want to see their research run in production, not just in a paper, will find it a good fit. What You'll Bring to the Team: Education: Currently enrolled in a PhD program in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Electrical Engineering or a related field, with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 and Spring 2029. Research experience: 2+ years of research experience in machine learning or ML systems, including hands-on work with large language models: training or fine-tuning (SFT, RLHF, DPO, GRPO/PPO) or inference optimization. Programming: Strong Python and PyTorch; comfortable reading and modifying large ML codebases. Experimental rigor: You design controlled experiments, choose the right baselines and metrics, and can tell a real effect from noise. Systems awareness: Working knowledge of how LLM training and inference run on GPUs, such as batching, memory, mixed precision and parallelism. Communication: You explain complex results clearly in writing and in person, and you work well with engineers turning research into product. Bonus Points Publications at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys, ACL, EMNLP or COLM on RL for LLMs, reward modeling, agents, efficient training or efficient inference. Hands-on experience with inference engines (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) or training frameworks (verl, OpenRLHF, TRL, Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed). Experience with quantization, speculative decoding, GPU kernels (CUDA, Triton) or LoRA/PEFT methods. Experience building agent environments, tool-use sandboxes or evaluation harnesses. We’re backed by founders and operators behind some of the most legendary tech companies of our time, Tier-1 U.S. venture firms, and board members of global industrial companies. ERPs ran the physical world for half a century. Dryft is building the intelligence layer that will power the next. ​ THE ROLE As our Founders Associate Intern , you'll step into the shoes of a founder. You'll own the highest-priority projects across product, sales, hiring or operations. One day you're on site with a client, the next you're building a new prototype, and in between you're hosting a hackathon for the best builders in the city. Work on what matters most – whatever the founders are in the middle of, you take it off their plate and own it end-to-end Build from zero – launch the things that don't exist yet at Dryft, from a new market entry to prototypes to our next event Fast-track your career – prove yourself across every part of the company, and grow into a full-time role in Deployment, Growth or Special Projects You'll learn how a company gets built, from the inside, at full speed. And yes, this will be the hardest internship you've ever had. ​ YOU Fast-paced experience – 2-3 internships in a top-tier role (e.g., consulting), at a high-growth startup, or you've built something of your own Founder DNA – you have high agency, drive and a serious work ethic; you thrive in ambiguity and anticipate next priorities instead of waiting for direction Learning at full speed – you're useful in week one and indispensable by week four Competitive by nature – you've won at something hard, and you're not done winning Gets shit done & zero ego – you move fast, figure things out, and you'd rather ship it than get the credit Language – you speak native-level German and fluent English Relocation – you're ready to work onsite in Munich

We're building toward the agentic investment banking capabilities for the era of digital finance. A proprietary agentic layer runs the mechanics of the market, so our people can focus on the work code cannot do: the deal, the relationship, and the judgement. We're not just envisioning the future of finance - we're building it. Data Analytics & Monitoring: Query on-chain data, EVM event logs, and lending protocol data using SQL, Subgraphs, and Python to generate actionable insights for credit positioning and risk allocation. Protocol Due Diligence & Forensics: Perform quantitative forensics and stress testing on emerging lending primitives, liquid staking protocols, and structured credit products prior to capital deployment. Who You Are/Key Requirements Technical & Quantitative Skills: Strong code-first foundation in Python, familiarity with Rust with Solidity as a plus. Understanding of smart contract mechanics and DeFi primitive mathemtaics (including propAMMs, lending pool utilization curves, liquidation thresholds). Quantitative & Trading Mindset: Rigorous background in a quantitative field (Math, Physics, CS, Finance, or Engineering) with a systematic/trading mindset. Ability to model yield dynamics, credit risk, backtesting strategies, and protocol insolvency scenarios. DeFi “Skin in the Game”: Hands-on experience interacting with decentralized lending protocols (e.g., Aave, Morpho, Compound, Maker/Endgame), yield aggregators, or credit markets. Nice-to-Haves: Familiarity with Rust, Solidity, Foundry, or specialized credit risk models and backtesting frameworks. description: About Parspec Founded in 2021, Parspec is revolutionizing the materials supply chain for the $13 trillion USD construction industry by digitizing and organizing the industry's product data. Our proprietary AI technology maintains a current and comprehensive catalogue of millions of products, enabling our customers to instantly identify the products that best meet their needs. Trusted by top designers, builders, distributors, manufacturers, and sales agents, and backed by leading venture investors, Parspec is paving the way for a more innovative, connected, and sustainable future in construction. Join us in building transformative technology that reshapes one of the world's oldest and largest industries. The Opportunity What does it take to turn an AI agent into a product customers trust and pay for? That question sits at the heart of this internship. We are looking for an intern to work alongside Parspec's product leadership on our AI quoting agent, the product at the center of how distributors and rep agencies build quotes. You will own a piece of it end to end, from customer discovery through an engineering-ready product spec, and help shape the business model behind it. Quoting is the beating heart of our customers' business. It is also messy, manual, and full of judgment calls, which is exactly what makes it both a hard and a valuable problem for an AI agent to take on. This is not a shadowing role. You will talk to real customers, write requirements that engineers build against, and build prototypes. If you see yourself becoming an AI product leader or founding a company someday, this is a chance to work on the two problems that define AI product management right now: making agents reliable and making them commercially viable. What You Will Achieve and Key Responsibilities Define what to build Interview distributor and rep agency users to understand how quotes get built today, step by step, including the workarounds and judgment calls that never show up in a process diagram Map the quoting workflow end to end and identify where an AI agent delivers the most value, and where human judgment needs to stay in the loop Turn what you learn into a clear, prioritized view of what the agent should do next, backed by customer evidence rather than intuition Prototype and validate Build working prototypes to test agent workflows with real users before engineering commits to a full build Translate customer needs into product requirements and an engineering-ready spec for your piece of the agent Define the success metrics that tell us the agent is actually working: accuracy, time saved, trust, and adoption Set the release criteria the agent must meet before it reaches customers, including how we evaluate reliability on real-world quoting scenarios Shape AI pricing Analyze the value the agent creates for customers, how usage actually behaves, and what it costs us to serve Study how other AI products charge for agentic work, from seats to usage to outcomes, and what those models would mean for our customers and our margins Recommend how Parspec should charge for AI-powered work, with the analysis to back it up, and present it to leadership Why This Matters Every software company is racing to put AI agents in front of customers. Very few have figured out the two things that actually matter: making the agent reliable enough that customers trust it with real work, and pricing it so the business works. Parspec is live in the market with AI doing real quoting work for real customers, which means these are not thought experiments here. The quality bar you set shapes what customers experience, and the pricing model you recommend shapes how the company grows. Few internships put you that close to the decisions that matter. Who You Are You are curious about how products get built and sold. You like talking to users as much as you like working through data, and you can hold both the customer's reality and the business model in your head at the same time. You write clearly, you ask sharp questions, and you are comfortable forming a view on a problem nobody has fully solved yet. This internship offers a unique opportunity to translate cutting-edge research ideas into real-world systems that safeguard millions of developers worldwide. You will contribute to the design and implementation of large-scale data collection and analysis pipelines, conduct in-depth investigations of malicious activity in open source ecosystems, and prototype novel techniques for detecting fraud and abuse on platforms such as GitHub. We are interested in research on any aspect of software supply chain security. As one of our research interns, you will not only push the boundaries of software supply chain security but also help shape the culture and direction of a fast-growing security company. This role is ideal for PhD students eager to bridge academia and industry and bring innovative research into production environments while gaining hands-on development experience in a high-impact, mission-driven setting. You can read more about Socket Labs here . What You'll Do Conduct applied research on emerging threats in the software supply chain (e.g., self-propagating malware in package ecosystems, dependency hallucinations, AI emerging threats) and translate findings into detection prototypes and publish the results. Design and evaluate novel algorithms for identifying malicious or inauthentic activity across ecosystems such as npm, PyPI, and GitHub. Leverage data science and machine learning techniques to model suspicious publishing behaviors, coordinated activity, and fraud campaigns. Develop automated research tools to collect, transform, and analyze large-scale datasets from third-party APIs (e.g., npm, GitHub, PyPI). Prototype and validate detection systems that can be integrated into Socket’s threat intelligence platform, bridging research insights with production impact. Collaborate with engineers and designers to experiment with new ways of surfacing research findings in user-facing interfaces and developer workflows. Publish research outputs internally (dashboards, reports, proofs-of-concept) to influence product strategy and publish papers in conferences/share with the broader research community. Contribute to the early team culture, bringing a research-driven perspective to technical discussions, prioritization, and the company’s long-term vision. Strong background in one or more of the following research areas: software supply chain security, program analysis, or AI security. Proficiency with languages commonly used for prototyping and research (e.g., JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, or similar). Familiarity with software and systems security concepts, such as threat modeling, malware analysis, or adversarial behavior in open ecosystems. Experience conducting research involving data analysis, statistical methods, and experimental evaluation. Strong analytical and creative problem-solving skills; able to explore novel approaches and rigorously evaluate their effectiveness. Self-motivated and comfortable driving independent research while collaborating with an interdisciplinary team. Strong written and verbal communication skills for presenting research findings and collaborating across engineering and design. Experience with publishing research at top-tier academic conferences, like IEEE S&P, USENIX Security, CCS, and NDSS. Prior work in one or more of the following is a plus: Static/dynamic analysis of software or binaries Open source security research Experience with Socket-supported ecosystems Vulnerability discovery Building scalable data pipelines or visualization dashboards Hiring is a big decision on both sides. Work Arrangement

This is an onsite position.

Job Overview

The Naval Architecture Intern supports vessel design, analysis, modeling, and engineering activities across a diverse portfolio of maritime programs. Working under the guidance of experienced naval architects and marine engineers, this position provides hands-on exposure to vessel design, hydrostatics, hydrodynamics, stability, structures, and marine operations while contributing to real-world engineering projects.

 

Essential Functions

  • Assist with vessel design studies, concept development activities, and engineering analyses.
  • Support hydrostatic, stability, resistance and powering, seakeeping, and vessel performance evaluations.
  • Develop and modify vessel arrangements, engineering drawings, and 3D models under engineering supervision.
  • Assist in preparing technical reports, calculations, engineering documentation, presentations, and design packages.
  • Support evaluation of vessel layouts, compartment arrangements, mission payload integration, and equipment installations.
  • Assist with structural assessments and engineering analyses using established naval architecture methods and tools.
  • Support application of classification society, customer, and regulatory requirements to vessel designs.
  • Participate in design reviews, engineering discussions, and multidisciplinary project meetings.
  • Collect, organize, and analyze engineering data from vessels, simulations, models, tests, and field activities.
  • Support dockside inspections, vessel surveys, sea trials, testing, and verification activities as assigned.
  • Document engineering observations, findings, lessons learned, and technical recommendations.
  • Collaborate with naval architecture, mechanical, electrical, systems, software, and production personnel on engineering tasks.
  • Learn and apply company engineering processes, configuration management practices, documentation standards, and technical procedures.
  • Perform other duties as assigned in support of engineering and maritime operations.

Standard Essential Functions

  • Regular and reliable attendance on a full time basis [or in accordance with posted schedule].
  • Responsible for exhibiting professional behavior with both internal and external business associates that reflects positively on the company and is consistent with the company's policies and practices.
  • Embodies AEVEX’s cultural values and aligns daily actions with department goals and company culture.

 

Qualifications            

  • Fundamental understanding of naval architecture and marine engineering principles.
  • Coursework exposure to hydrostatics, hydrodynamics, fluid mechanics, statics, dynamics, or related engineering disciplines.
  • Familiarity with vessel stability, resistance and powering, seakeeping, structures, arrangements, or marine systems.
  • Basic understanding of engineering drawing interpretation and technical documentation practices.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to document technical work clearly and effectively.
  • Ability to learn new engineering tools, methods, and processes.
  • Ability to receive technical guidance and incorporate feedback from experienced engineers.
  • Ability to work both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary engineering team.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Interest in maritime systems, vessel design, and marine operations.
  • Ability to safely board and traverse vessels, docks, shipyards, and waterfront facilities.
  • Ability and willingness to work in office, laboratory, manufacturing, shipyard, waterfront, and vessel environments.
  • Ability to occasionally lift, carry, and transport engineering equipment and materials consistent with job requirements.
  • Ability and willingness to travel occasionally in support of testing, inspections, sea trials, and project activities.
  • Preferred:
    • Familiarity with vessel arrangements, stability analysis, resistance and powering, seakeeping, or marine structures.
    • Familiarity with marine industry standards and classification society requirements, including ABS, DNV, USCG, or U.S. Navy guidance.

Education / Certifications

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Naval Architecture, Ocean Engineering, Marine Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
  • Completion of coursework in engineering fundamentals such as statics, dynamics, fluid mechanics, naval architecture, or related technical subjects.
  • Preferred:
    • Completion of junior- or senior-level coursework in Naval Architecture, Ocean Engineering, or Marine Engineering.
    • Relevant academic projects, undergraduate research, engineering competitions, or design-team participation related to maritime systems.
    • Training or coursework involving vessel design, stability analysis, marine structures, hydrodynamics, or marine systems engineering.

Experience

  • No professional experience required.
  • Academic coursework demonstrating engineering fundamentals applicable to vessel design and marine systems.
  • Experience participating in engineering projects, laboratory work, design teams, research activities, or technical extracurricular programs.
  • Experience preparing engineering calculations, technical reports, presentations, or design documentation.</

Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Airbnb is excited to welcome Software Engineering Interns for our 2027 Summer Intern Program from May 24, 2027 - August 13, 2027.

At Airbnb, we believe technology has the power to bring people together — and our engineers are the ones building it. Our Engineering org is a diverse, fast-moving group of teams working across Payments, Trust, Marketing, Relevance & Personalization, and more. Together, we're tackling some of the hardest problems in tech: search relevance at global scale, fraud prevention, seamless payments, and fueling growth — all while delivering a product experience that feels effortless and beautiful. We're also at the forefront of integrating AI and machine learning into our products — from personalized search experiences to intelligent trust and safety systems — and we're looking for curious engineers who are excited to grow alongside this technology.

description:
About AppLovin

AppLovin makes technologies that help businesses of every size connect to their ideal customers. The company provides end-to-end advertising solutions for businesses to reach, monetize and grow their global audiences. For more information about AppLovin, visit: www.applovin.com.

To deliver on this mission, our global team is composed of team members with life experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives that mirror our developers and customers around the world. At AppLovin, we are intentional about the team and culture we are building, seeking candidates who are outstanding in their own right and also demonstrate their support of others.

About Gist

Gist is a new consumer social app built by AppLovin, a handbook for the curious. We’re building a lifestyle platform for adults 25–45 around the relatable, actionable content people use to navigate their daily lives: food, wellness, fashion, family, and personal finance. We’re building our creator ecosystem from the ground up, and we’re looking for an intern to help us find the talent that will define it.

The best outcome of this internship is seeing the partnerships you build contribute to Gist’s growth.


About the Role

This is a research and pipeline role sitting at the center of our platform partnerships team. You won’t be filing decks or sitting in on calls. You’ll be doing the ground-level work that makes creator partnership recruitment possible: finding the right talent, agency, growth platforms, tracking outreach, and keeping our partnership database sharp and current.


A Day in the Life

  • Research and identify potential partners across creators, brands, agencies, and communities that can help grow Gist
  • Support partner outreach by drafting communications, coordinating follow-ups, and tracking responses
  • Maintain our partnership pipeline, keeping contacts, opportunities, status, and next steps organized and up to date
  • Evaluate potential partners based on audience fit, strategic relevance, and growth potential
  • Surface emerging trends and partnership opportunities that could strengthen Gist’s content, community, and reach
  • Build and automate workflows using AI tools to improve research, outreach, and pipeline management
  • Track and report on partnership performance using data and KPIs to measure impact on Gist’s growth

 

Who You Are

  • Bachelor’s degree or above in Science, Computer Science, Business or any related fields graduating December 2027 or Spring 2028
  • Strong AI skills and genuine interest in building automation workflows
  • Comfortable with data: you think in metrics, track what you do, and can connect your work to measurable outcomes
  • A clear, confident communicator who adapts quickly and is receptive to feedback
  • Curious about how platform partnerships work: the deal structures, the pitch, the relationship-building
  • Sharp, flexible thinker who can pivot quickly as priorities shift
  • Prior experience in influencer marketing, talent management, or creator-focused roles is a plus


Why Join

  • A front-row seat to how a well-funded platform builds its creator ecosystem from zero
  • Direct exposure to the full creator partnership lifecycle: sourcing, outreach, negotiation, and onboarding
  • Mentorship from a senior creator partnerships team with deep roots in talent agencies and management
  • Real, meaningful work from day one: the creators you find could end up shaping what Gist becomes
  • Opportunity for full-time conversion for exceptional performers

description:
What we’re building

The marine industry supports recreation, global commerce, and national defense. And yet it runs on technology that hasn't meaningfully changed in fifty years. Until now.

Arc is on a mission to electrify the marine industry. We're rethinking powertrains, software, and vessel designs from first principles. And we're already executing. We started with consumers to develop and harden our core technology. We’re now scaling production of our flagship model with new models and sectors on the horizon. Now we’re extending our platform to commercial applications, starting with tugs, ferries, and defense, with years worth of signed contracts and a pipeline that spans every vessel type on the water.

The technology is proven, the momentum is building, and the opportunity is enormous. The marine industry is going electric and Arc is building the platform that powers it

Who we’re looking for

We’re looking for a hands-on, curious engineering student who wants to understand why things fail in the field and how to fix them for good. We pride ourselves on transparency and operate in a lean, high-trust environment that encourages everyone to take ownership over their domain.

You will be a full-time member of our Service team, will report directly to our service engineer and will work from our manufacturing facility in Los Angeles. Given that we’re a startup, you will be working in a fast-moving, dynamic environment that requires adaptability. That said, here are some responsibilities and qualifications we expect to stay relatively constant for this role.

What You'll Do

  • Developing and documenting standard repair processes, work instructions, and troubleshooting guides for common field issues
  • Diagnosing field failures alongside Service and Vehicle Engineers, using boat data, logs, photos, and teardowns to find root causes
  • Structuring field failure data into a consistent format (failure mode, system, part, root cause, corrective action)
  • Reporting failure trends and recurring issues to engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams to support our quality initiative
  • Following up on corrective actions and refining repair procedures based on technician and engineer feedback

Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field
  • Comfortable with hands-on work around hardware, tools, and vehicles
  • Strong organization and attention to detail when structuring data and writing documentation
  • Proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets (pivot tables, charts, basic formulas)

Bonus Qualifications

  • Experience on a student engineering team (Formula SAE, Baja, solar car, robotics) or in a repair shop
  • Familiarity with root cause methods such as 5 Whys, 8D, FMEA, or Pareto analysis
  • Exposure to diagnostic tools (multimeter, CAN tools) or reading wiring diagrams; experience with Python, SQL, or BI tools
  • Comfortable pushing a fast but sustainable pace
  • Enthusiasm for boating and clean energy

At Arc, we encourage diversity and consider all qualified applicants equally for employment, regardless of background, identity, or status. You’re always welcome to reach out even if you don’t meet many of these qualifications. Passion and aptitude make up for a lot.

What we offer

The base pay for this role is $36 per hour. 

Additionally, as an Arc Intern, you'll also get:

  • Boat days – Yes, we actually go out on the water. A lot.
  • Retirement savings — Traditional and Roth 401(k) access
  • Safety support — Reimbursement for PPE, ergonomic equipment, and anything that ensures we keep our crew safe
  • Relocation Assistance
  • Mentorship Opportunities
  • Office perks — Daily lunches, snacks, and good coffee while onsite

Our values

We move with urgency and build with care. We value these five things above all else:

  • Ownership over both your work and the company’s success
  • Empathy for colleagues and for customers
  • Humility in problem solving and collaboration
  • Pragmatism for navigating ambiguity quickly and sensibly 
  • Inclusion of different backgrounds, opinions, cultures, and perspectives.

We want people who share and embody these values. It is vital that our values align - we’d be happy to elaborate on any or all of these during the interview process.

  • Manage the Candidate Journey: Serve as a point of contact for candidates throughout the process, ensuring every touchpoint is timely, professional, and reflects Eulerity's brand.

  • Feedback Collection & Reporting

  • Talent Sourcing (Learning Track)
    • Go beyond LinkedIn. Learn to use GitHub, Stack Overflow, and technical communities to source passive engineering candidates. Develop a basic understanding of our tech stack to better qualify resumes and assess potential.

Who You Are

  • Currently pursuing a degree in Human Resources, Marketing, Business, Psychology, Communications, or something related and graduating no earlier than May 2027.

  • A Strong Communicator: You write and speak clearly and professionally, and you are comfortable interacting with candidates, hiring managers, and senior leaders alike.

Why Eulerity?

Quantitative Research Intern – Systematic FICC - Hong Kong

About the Team

The Systematic Rates team researches and runs fully systematic, data-driven strategies in global interest FICC markets. We combine solid statistics, careful engineering and a good feel for how markets work to build and improve systematic trading strategies.

The Role

You'll work closely with the portfolio manager. You'll do hands-on research and development across the whole strategy process, and you'll own real projects with real impact, not side tasks.

  • Research, prototype and backtest systematic strategies across FICC products such as swaps and foreign exchange.

About Pioneering Medicines

Pioneering Medicines, Flagship Pioneering’s in-house drug development unit, is dedicated to conceiving and developing a broad portfolio of life-changing treatments for patients built from Flagship’s innovative platforms. Harnessing the drug development expertise of its team together with the power of Flagship’s multiple scientific platforms, Pioneering Medicines explores and identifies new product concepts which are then advanced jointly with Flagship’s bioplatform companies. Within Flagship’s Innovation Supply Chain partnerships, Pioneering Medicines works with external collaborators to apply its unique approach to partners’ R&D priorities. These partnerships are highly co-creative strategic alliances that accelerate therapeutic innovation by bringing together partners spanning the full spectrum of drug discovery, development, and production.

About Flagship Pioneering

Pioneering Medicines was founded by Flagship Pioneering's venture creation engine that invents and builds platform companies, each with the potential for multiple products that transform human health or sustainability. Since its launch in 2000, Flagship has originated and fostered more than 100 scientific ventures, resulting in more than $90 billion in aggregate value. Many of the company’s Flagship has founded have addressed humanity’s most urgent challenges: vaccinating billions of people against COVID-19, curing intractable diseases, improving human health, preempting illness, and feeding the world by improving the resiliency and sustainability of agriculture. Flagship has been recognized twice on FORTUNE’s “Change the World” list, an annual ranking of companies that have made a positive social and environmental impact through activities that are part of their core business strategies and has been twice named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies. Learn more about Flagship at www.flagshippioneering.com.

Flagship Pioneering Co-Op Program

Welcome to Flagship Pioneering Co-Op Program for the cohort dreaming big and taking courageous leaps. You'll join fellow peers across our ecosystem of companies and learning firsthand how we build first-in-category companies. You’ll have access to enrichment sessions, a dedicated professional development track, and a mentor that help guide you toward your next step. By the end, you will carry on a meaningful project outcome, a genuine network, and a front-row view of how Flagship pioneer new ventures that change the world.

Position Description 

We are seeking a motivated Drug Substance Co-Op with a chemical, biochemical, or biomedical engineering background and hands-on skill in in silico modeling of unit operations. This role will support Drug Substance process development in the CMC and Bioprocess Development group, using mechanistic and data-driven models to guide process design, scale-up, and tech transfer for biologics, small molecules, and peptides.

Reporting to a Drug Substance process development lead, the co-op will work alongside upstream, downstream, analytical, and regulatory CMC colleagues and gain exposure to our network of CDMO partners. The co-op is a chance to apply engineering fundamentals to live programs and see how modeling decisions shape real manufacturing processes.

The co-op is expected to run >6 mo. or part-time during the academic year, with a defined project and an end-of-term presentation to the CMC team.

Key Responsibilities

In Silico Unit Operation Modeling

  • Build, calibrate, and run models of drug substance unit operations (for example, cell culture and fermentation, chromatography, ultrafiltration/diafiltration, viral inactivation and filtration, crystallization, and peptide synthesis and purification) using mechanistic, hybrid, or statistical approaches.
  • Use models to evaluate operating ranges, identify sensitive process parameters, and compare scale-up and scale-down options.
  • Run sensitivity analyses and simulation-based studies to support process characterization and design-space thinking.

Data Analysis & Process Understanding

  • Collect, clean, and analyze lab, pilot, and CDMO batch data to fit and verify models.
  • Apply statistical tools and design of experiments (DoE) to plan and interpret studies.
  • Summarize model results, assumptions, and limitations in clear technical reports and presentations.

Tech Transfer & CDMO Support

  • Support tech transfer by translating model outputs into process descriptions, parameter ranges, and risk assessments for CDMO partners.
  • Help review batch records and process data from external manufacturing sites and flag deviations from model predictions.

Join Lightmatter’s Packaging team to build the foundation of an AI-enabled framework that lets engineers quickly explore package design options and narrow candidates before committing to detailed simulation or hardware builds. You’ll combine physics-based simulation with machine learning, including physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and other surrogate models, to make fast early predictions that stay physically grounded. Initial use cases include narrowing thermal solutions and predicting warpage, with room to extend to other objectives. 

Your work will feed into all upcoming products, POCs, and test vehicles from day one, and your experiments will build fundamental understanding of coupled thermal-structural-optical physics. You’ll be mentored by experienced thermal and thermo-mechanical engineers and learn how first-order analysis, AI surrogates, and high-fidelity simulation complement each other in early design decisions, and how package architecture, materials, and cooling come together in leading-edge AI and HPC products.

Responsibilities:

  • Build a flexible framework that links package design parameters (geometry, materials, process, thermal solution) to outputs such as thermal performance and warpage.

  • Automate FEA and CFD setup, execution, and post-processing in Python to generate parametric datasets. Train and validate models against high-fidelity simulation and hardware data, quantifying accuracy and uncertainty.
  • Plan and run physical DOEs (test setup, measurement, analysis) to build understanding of coupled thermal-structural-optical physics.
  • Partner with packaging, thermal, and thermo-mechanical engineers to define requirements and inputs/outputs, and adapt the framework to upcoming products.

  • Currently pursuing an MS or PhD in Mechanical Engineering or a related field.
  • Coursework in heat transfer, fluid mechanics, FEA, CFD, numerical methods, and solid or fracture mechanics.

Track 2 — Agentic SSR (AI and Server-Side Rendering): Build the server-rendered, agentic layer of the Lila Platform — the infrastructure that enables AI agents to compose and serve dynamic scientific interfaces at runtime.

Lila runs autonomous science facilities — labs full of instruments, robotics, and controllers that produce the experimental data that is the company's core IP. Securing that environment is a different problem from securing laptops and SaaS, and we are building the program from the ground up. This co-op works on that build, not on the side of it.

The role sits at the seam between IT, Lab IT, and OT, spanning four workstreams: OT asset visibility and tooling, vulnerability and patch management across IT/OT, SOC integration and threat intelligence, and program build. The work product outlives the term.

description:
Power Electronics Test Intern

Lunar Energy builds home energy products that make clean power abundant and accessible: inverters, batteries, and the software that ties them together. As a Power Electronics Test Intern, you will test those products, from the first bench measurement to the certification report. Your work covers two jobs that usually sit apart: power electronics performance testing, and compliance testing for safety, grid interconnection, and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). You will work on inverters, batteries, energy storage systems, and electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE, or EV chargers), in our high-voltage lab, alongside design, firmware, reliability, and manufacturing engineers. What you find will change what we ship.

What you will gain: Gain practical experience in designing and testing Lunar’s products, while developing a comprehensive understanding of the full lifecycle from design to validation and certification. You will collaborate closely with design engineers, observe how testing data directly informs engineering decisions, and deliver key insights derived from test results and rigorous data analysis.

Lunar Energy was founded to transition homes to 100% clean energy—making our electricity greener, our air cleaner and our energy more safe, secure and reliable for all. We’re a fast-growing, global company building the world’s best clean energy products to electrify all homes and connect communities to form clean, resilient virtual power plants.

On a given day at Lunar, you’ll likely…

  • Test inverters, batteries, energy storage systems, and EVSE for efficiency, power quality, protection response, fault behavior, transients, and thermal performance
  • Run compliance and pre-compliance tests against safety, grid interconnection, and EMC standards, and help prepare products for testing for  certification.
  • Work with Compliance Engineers, & write test plans and procedures that trace each test back to a clause in the standard it supports.
  • Build and run test setups with grid simulators, programmable AC and DC sources, battery cyclers, electronic loads, power analyzers, oscilloscopes, EV simulators, and environmental chambers.
  • Automate test sequences and data processing in Python so a test that takes a day by hand takes an hour.
  • Design targeted experiments to isolate failure modes, then diagnose them and drive root cause analysis with corrective and preventive actions.
  • Analyze test data, report findings clearly, and bring early compliance risks to design reviews before they become redesigns. Review engineering changes for their effect on existing certifications
  • Keep detailed records of tests, analyses, and corrective actions, and prepare test reports and technical files for internal teams and outside certification bodies.
  • Work with design, firmware, reliability, and manufacturing engineers to protect design integrity and inform design decisions.

 

Desired Skills:

Required

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Electrical Engineering or a closely related field (Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Aerospace Engineering, or Physics) or recently graduated.
  • Strong grasp of electrical engineering fundamentals: AC power, three-phase systems, power converters (AC/DC, DC/DC, DC/AC), and basic control and protection concepts.
  • Hands-on lab experience with oscilloscopes, power supplies, multimeters, and current and voltage probes.
  • Experience with Python, C, or C++, and with processing and plotting measurement data.
  • Strong debugging instincts: you can isolate a failure mode, design an experiment, and close a finding with a documented root cause.
  • Careful, safety-minded work habits, with the discipline that high-voltage lab work demands.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining a technical result to both engineers and non-engineers.
  • Comfort with ambiguity, a fast pace, and working across teams and with outside labs. 
  • An ownership mindset: you follow a problem through to the end

Preferred

  • Coursework or project experience in power electronics, grid-connected inverters, battery systems, or EV charging
  • Familiarity with safety and grid standards for energy products, such as UL 1741, IEEE 1547, UL 1973, UL 9540
  • Familiarity with EMC testing and standards, such as FCC Part 15, and IEC 61000: conducted and radiated emissions, electrostatic discharge, electrical fast transient, and surge immunity
  • Experience with automated test systems, such as instrument control with SCPI, PyVISA.
  • Experience with battery testing (cycling, thermal chambers) or with reliability, abuse, or environmental stress testing.
  • Data analysis and visualization experience in Python.
  • Prior lab research in power electronics, energy storage, or high-voltage systems
  • Comfort using AI tools to speed up analysis and documentation, with the judgment to check their output and protect confidential data.

Investment and Trading Intern

Duration: 10 weeks | Location: Hong Kong | Reports to: Head of Asia Treasury

About the role

Marshall Wace's Asia Treasury team is looking for a technically minded undergraduate to spend 10 weeks mapping, documenting and improving the workflows that underpin Treasury operations in Hong Kong. You will sit at the intersection of Treasury, Operations, Execution and Technology -- learning how processes, systems and teams connect across the firm while producing practical outputs the team will use long after the internship ends.

No prior Treasury experience is required. What matters is curiosity about how complex systems work, comfort with data, and the ability to communicate clearly -- especially when turning a messy process into a clean diagram or document. You will report to the Head of Asia Treasury and work with colleagues across multiple functions, gaining broad exposure to how a systematic hedge fund operates day to day.

Responsibilities

  • Map Treasury workflows and system dependencies across the MWAM ecosystem, including Posh, MATE tables, ECCO, broker data files and margin calls
  • Document key triggers, hand-offs and reconciliation points for core Treasury activities such as margin management, payments, funding and FX hedging
  • Identify manual steps, data gaps and opportunities for automation within existing processes
  • Prototype a reconciliation tool or dashboard using sample data where appropriate
  • Present findings to the team and deliver documentation suitable for onboarding and future process improvement

Requirements

  • Undergraduate pursuing a degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics, statistics, quantitative finance or a related discipline, graduating in 2028
  • Comfortable working with data; familiarity with Python, SQL or data visualisation tools is a plus
  • Strong written communication skills with the ability to explain complex processes visually through diagrams and documentation
  • Organised, self-directed and curious, with a willingness to ask questions and explore unfamiliar systems
  • Interest in financial markets and how technology supports trading operations
  • Eligible to work in Hong Kong for the duration of the 10-week internship

About Pinterest:

Millions of people around the world come to our platform to find creative ideas, dream about new possibilities and plan for memories that will last a lifetime. At Pinterest, we’re on a mission to bring everyone the inspiration to create a life they love, and that starts with the people behind the product.

Discover a career where you ignite innovation for millions, transform passion into growth opportunities, celebrate each other’s unique experiences and embrace the flexibility to do your best work. Creating a career you love? It’s Possible.

At Pinterest, AI isn't just a feature, it's a powerful partner that augments our creativity and amplifies our impact, and we’re looking for candidates who are excited to be a part of that. To get a complete picture of your experience and abilities, we’ll explore your foundational skills and how you collaborate with AI.

Through our interview process, what matters most is that you can always explain your approach, showing us not just what you know, but how you think. You can read more about our AI interview philosophy and how we use AI in our recruiting process here.

The Sales Strategy & Operations team partners with advertising sales leaders to improve business performance and help the sales organization make informed decisions. As a Sales Analytics Intern, you’ll help turn data into insights that support sales performance, planning, and day-to-day decisions. You’ll contribute to reporting, analysis, and process-improvement projects while building your skills in communication and cross-functional collaboration.

What you’ll do:

  • Analyze data related to pipeline health, sales performance, coverage, productivity, forecasting, and planning.
  • Build or improve recurring reports and dashboards, check data quality, and make insights clear and useful for business partners.
  • Explore performance trends across regions, products, segments, or sales motions; identify possible drivers, data gaps, and follow-up questions.
  • Turn analyses into concise summaries, presentations, and recommendations that help teammates understand findings and decide on next steps.
  • Support straightforward planning or scenario analyses using established assumptions, templates, and guidance from the team.
  • Partner with Sales, Finance, Marketing, and other teams to clarify business questions, align on metrics, and respond to analytical requests.
  • Document reporting workflows, identify manual steps, and suggest practical process improvements.
  • Thoughtfully use approved AI tools to support research, analysis, documentation, or workflow improvements and validate outputs before sharing them.

What we’re looking for:

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in business, economics, statistics, data analytics or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Ability to analyze data, identify patterns and explain findings and implications clearly. You can structure analytical questions, break work into manageable steps, ask clarifying questions and communicate conclusions.
  • Proficiency with Excel or Google Sheets to organize data, conduct analysis or build basic models.
  • Familiarity with SQL and at least one analytics or visualization tool such as Tableau, Looker or Power BI gained through coursework, projects or internships.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to summarize findings for technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Interest in sales analytics, digital advertising, revenue operations or go-to-market strategy.
  • Capacity to collaborate, manage agreed upon priorities and make progress on assigned projects.
  • Ability to use AI tools responsibly to support research or analysis, check outputs against source data and business context and take ownership of the final work.

In-Office Requirement:

  • We recognize that the ideal environment for work is situational and may differ across departments. 
  • What this looks like day-to-day can vary based on the needs of each organization or role. This role will need to be in the office for in-person collaboration 1-3 times per week and therefore needs to be within a commutable distance of San Francisco or NYC. 
  • This internship is full-time during typical business hours, Monday through Friday.

Relocation Statement:

  • This position may be eligible for relocation assistance. Visit our PinFlex page to learn more about our working model.
  • Information regarding the culture at Pinterest and benefits available for this position can be found here.

We offer 2 internship start dates:

  • May 17, 2027 - August 6, 2027
  • June 14, 2027 - September 3, 2027 

US based applicants only

Operations

The Trade Support team, part of Operations, supports the operational aspects of trade processing, reconciliation, financing, and reporting for all products across global markets - equities, derivatives, bonds, foreign exchange, and futures. About Re:Build 

At Re:Build, our mission is to ensure the next generation of important products are made, at scale, in America. We are laying the foundation for a better future for our customers, employees, and communities by revitalizing America's manufacturing base and creating meaningful jobs across the country, including in historically deindustrialized regions. 

We operate an advanced, end-to-end manufacturing platform that partners with industrial companies and innovators to take products from first concept to full-scale production in critical verticals including aerospace and defense, electrification, medical, energy and environment, and robotics and automation. 

The way we operate is as important as the work we do. It's guided by The Re:Build Way, 16 principles that shape how we collaborate with each other, partner with our customers and vendors, and contribute to the communities where we operate. (link to The Re:Build Way principles) 

About Re:Build Optimation

At Re:Build Optimation, we specialize in delivering custom-engineered process equipment and automated systems to clients across the globe. With nearly 40 years of experience in complex chemical process systems, we have built a reputation for precision, reliability, and innovation. Our multidisciplinary team of 70+ engineers, designers, and programmers, combined with 150,000 square feet of fabrication space and over 70 skilled tradespeople, allows us to provide full turnkey solutions—from initial concept through fabrication, installation, and commissioning.

As part of Re:Build Manufacturing, we leverage the strength of a national industrial powerhouse while maintaining the agility and personalized service of a specialized firm. We serve industries ranging from traditional and green energy to chemicals, pharmaceuticals, food & beverage, glass, and advanced manufacturing, offering tailored solutions that optimize efficiency and performance.

We believe in a collaborative approach, working closely with our clients to develop solutions that align with their unique operational goals. Our deep industry expertise and end-to-end capabilities make us the ideal partner for companies seeking cutting-edge automation, process control, and engineered systems.

Who We Are Looking For

Re:Build Optimation is looking for a motivated Apprentice Industrial Welder who enjoys hands-on work and wants to build a career in skilled trades. If you have a strong work ethic, an interest in welding, and a desire to develop your craftsmanship, this is an opportunity to learn while you earn.

This entry-level position is part of a four-year New York State-accredited apprenticeship program combining on-the-job training with classroom instruction. You'll receive performance evaluations every six months, with wage increases following satisfactory reviews, and earn a Journey Worker Certificate upon successful completion.

Schedule: Monday–Friday, 6:00 a.m.–2:30 p.m., with flexibility for overtime and occasional travel.

What You Get To Do

  • Learn industrial welding techniques through hands-on training and classroom instruction.
  • Join metal components using electric arc-welding equipment and established welding procedures.
  • Read and interpret blueprints, diagrams, layouts, and work orders to complete welding assignments.
  • Set up and adjust welding equipment, including cables, amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse settings.
  • Develop safe work practices for construction and industrial environments.
  • Build your technical skills and craftsmanship under the guidance of expert professionals.

What You Bring To The Team

  • High school diploma or equivalent (GED or TASC).
  • Completion of one year of Algebra or equivalent.
  • Strong work ethic, willingness to learn, and interest in skilled trades.
  • Ability to climb, work at heights and in confined spaces, and lift or move heavy objects.
  • Ability to work in hot, cold, and varying weather conditions.
  • Reliable transportation to work and classroom training.
  • Flexibility to work overtime and travel occasionally.
  • Ability to pass a drug test and background check.
  • Preferred: Mechanical aptitude or experience working with tools and equipment.

The hourly rate for this position is $17.00 - $25.54. This range represents the Company’s good faith estimate of the base compensation for this role at the time of posting.  Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including but not limited to relevant experience, skills, qualifications, internal equity, and geographic location. In addition to hourly rate, this role may be eligible for annual incentive compensation and/or long-term incentives, subject to Company plans. The Company offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, retirement, paid time off, and other benefits

The BIG payoff

We are a company who is going to make a difference in the industries and the communities in which we choose to operate.  Every employee of Re:Build will share ownership in the company and will share in the financial rewards of the success we achieve together, at all levels of the company!

We want to work with people that reflect the communities in which we operate.

Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators. 

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there. 

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

As a Software Engineer Intern on our Engine team, you will be mentored by industry veterans from the video game and real-time simulation sectors. Over 12 weeks, we will provide you with a project tailored to your interests and our needs, focusing on your personal and professional development while you contribute to the core technology that powers millions of immersive experiences.


You Will:

  • Join our supportive Engine team, collaborating directly with and receiving mentorship from top-tier engineers on live projects.
  • Contribute code to our in-house proprietary game engine on the Rendering, Geometry, Avatar, or Physics Teams.
  • Our cross-platform rendering engine which supports APIs like DirectX, Vulkan, Metal, and OpenGL.
  • Our real-time physics engine simulates complex rigid body dynamics and environmental effects using fast numerical methods and high performance implementations.
  • Work on a meaningful project for the full internship, from design to implementation, focused on areas like graphics performance, new visual features, or real-time dynamic systems.
  • Learn about the unique challenges of rendering at a massive scale, where content is entirely user-generated.
  • Present your work and its impact to your team and leaders across the company at the end of your internship.

You Are:

  • Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Proficient in C++, as it is the primary language for our engine development.
  • Passionate about real-time computer graphics, rendering techniques, or related fields like physics and fluid simulations, demonstrated through coursework or personal projects.
  • Familiar with 3D math, numerical methods, physics and/or computer graphics fundamentals.
  • Excited about learning and crafting amazing experiences as you work with your team to reach collective goals.
  • As a Software Engineer Intern, we'll support you as you tackle the hardest problems in tech today – distributed systems, real-time communication, 3D co-experience, extensive data processing, social networking, rendering, physics, over the course of 12-weeks.

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

  • Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events

 

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS

Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results.

  • Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in an engineering, physics or math discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship
  • GPA of 3.0 or above
  • 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable)

 

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE

  • GPA of 3.5 or above
  • 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable)
  • Manufacturing engineering experience 
  • Python programming experience 
  • Six Sigma experience 

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 16 consecutive weeks beginning January 4, 2027.

COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS

  • You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs

The expected salary range for the position is displayed in accordance with the Ontario Pay Transparency Act. Final agreed upon compensation is based upon individual qualifications and experience.

Base salary is only one part of Rocket Lab’s compensation package for this role. You may be eligible for company stock, or cash incentives, and can purchase discounted stock through Rocket Lab’s Employee Stock Purchase Program. Employee benefits also include medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage; RRSP retirement plan options; paid vacation, holidays, and sick leave; paid parental leave; and other discounts and perks.

Base Pay Range (Ontario Only)
$60,008—$60,008 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT 

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. What You’ll Do

The Architecture Research Lab (ARL) is tackling two of the biggest challenges in AI today—memory bandwidth and communication bottlenecks. By leveraging Samsung’s world-leading memory technologies, we are developing next-generation AI systems that break through these limitations while improving developer productivity.

This internship explores how memory systems should evolve for agentic AI. AI agents work over long horizons, across many turns, and build up context faster than memory capacity and bandwidth grow. As a result, their accuracy and speed decline. You will research memory architectures and system optimizations that keep long-horizon inference accurate and efficient, evaluate them with performance models and accuracy studies, and turn the results into publications and into requirements for future memory products.

Advancing the World’s Technology Together

What You’ll Learn

  • Project Overview: In memory-centric AI accelerators, many memory devices each process data in place and only exchange small partial results, which are then merged. As LLM attention evolves from grouped-query attention (GQA) to multi-head latent attention (MLA) and sparse top-k attention, the work done locally on each device shrinks while cross-device merge and reduction increasingly dominate decode latency. description:
About Sezzle

With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We're not just transforming payments; we're redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we're building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you're excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!

About the Role

As a Fraud Operations Intern, you'll join our Shopper Risk Operations team, the people who keep Sezzle safe for shoppers and merchants. You'll review activity flagged by our fraud detection systems and Customer Support, decide what's fraud and what isn't, and help us spot new fraud patterns before they spread. You'll work alongside analysts, data scientists, and engineers, and see how fraud prevention works inside a fast-growing, publicly traded fintech.

We are seeking a talented and motivated intern who is best in class with a high IQ plus a high EQ. No prior fraud experience is required; we'll train you. Curiosity, attention to detail, and good judgment matter more.

This is a paid, full-time, remote internship: Monday to Friday, 12:00 pm to 21:00 pm local time.

What You'll Do

  • Review transactions and accounts flagged for possible fraud or abuse
  • Investigate cases using our internal tools and policies, and decide whether to block or clear them
  • Look for patterns in account and transaction data
  • Share what you find to help improve our fraud rules and detection models
  • Work through your case queue on time and keep clear notes
  • Help resolve escalations from internal teams

What You'll Learn

  • How fintech companies detect and prevent fraud, from manual review to machine learning models
  • How to investigate cases and make decisions with data
  • How risk, operations, data, and engineering teams work together

What We Look For

  • Current university student or recent graduate. Industrial or Systems Engineering, Economics, Business, Finance, Accounting, Statistics, Law, and related fields are a great fit
  • Strong attention to detail and good judgment
  • Comfortable working with numbers and spreadsheets (Excel or Google Sheets)
  • English at B2 level or higher (written and spoken)
  • Clear written communication
  • Able to work independently once trained
  • Comfortable using AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT to boost productivity, research, and communication

Nice to Have

  • Coursework or projects involving data analysis (Excel, SQL, or similar)
  • Interest in fintech, payments, or cybersecurity

About You

  • You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed.
  • You're not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things.
  • You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking.
  • You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.
  • You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly.
  • You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle.

What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome

At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators. We believe in surrounding ourselves with only the best and the brightest individuals. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire.

Compensation: The salary for the Fraud Operations Intern is $800 USD gross monthly.

This role: We are seeking a highly motivated Control Systems & Algorithms Co-op to join our team. We focus on developing real-time optimization and control algorithms for low-compute hardware that drive the next generation of smart household appliances. This role offers a hands-on opportunity to design, prototype, and validate control solutions that make appliances smarter, more efficient, and more reliable.

This co-op opportunity will provide valuable experience in the field of control systems engineering and mechatronics with a focus on programming skills, optimization, and algorithms development. If you are passionate and want to work on challenging projects, we encourage you to apply.

Here are some of the EXCITING things you’ll get to do:

  • Design and implement real-time control algorithms for appliance subsystems (thermal, fluidic, and electromechanical)
  • Work directly with pumps, heaters, boilers, AC/DC, and stepper motors, and their drivers
  • Interface with low-cost sensors (temperature, flow, pressure, torque, etc.) and implement signal processing, filtering, and estimation techniques (e.g., Kalman filters)
  • Apply classical control methods (frequency response analysis, PID design, and tuning) to achieve stability and robustness in systems with significant delays and nonlinearities
  • Rapidly build and iterate prototypes and test rigs to validate algorithms in real hardware environments
  • Collect and analyze experimental data to identify system dynamics and optimize performance
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to develop system design, software architecture, and bring control algorithms from concept to embedded deployment

 ATTRIBUTES & SKILLS: 

  • Education: Must be currently enrolled in a bachelor’s program (third year or beyond), master’s, or doctorate program
  • Must be able to work a full-time, 40-hour-per-week schedule with 5 days per week onsite in Needham, MA
  • Strong understanding of control system theory (frequency response, stability margins, PID design and tuning) and design, including classical control and advanced control
  • Proficiency in embedded C/C++ programming and experience with microcontrollers (e.g., STM32, ESP32, Arduino, or similar)
  • Familiarity with real-time signal processing and sensor fusion techniques
  • Comfort working hands-on with hardware systems (sensors, actuators, thermal and electromechanical components)
  • Strong problem-solving ability and willingness to prototype quickly and iterate
  • A natural and effective communicator capable of reducing abstract concepts to reality
  • Able to quickly generate visual and physical definitions of new products that convey key attributes of function
  • Naturally curious and relentlessly driven to find better solutions to everyday problems

Preferred/Bonus Qualifications:

  • Experience with MATLAB/Simulink for system modeling, state-space control, and model-based design (including Simulink Coder/code generation)
  • Background in system identification, including real-time or machine-learning-based modeling
  • Knowledge of nonlinear optimization algorithms suitable for low-compute, embedded environments
  • Familiarity with TinyML, CMSIS libraries, or other embedded ML frameworks
  • Experience with embedded system architecture and designing control soft

Who You Are:

Are you passionate about AI, and its potential to help accelerate science?

Ai2's Asta Project (https://allenai.org/asta) aims to rapidly advance science, developing solutions in the areas of AI research assistants for scientists, literature understanding and synthesis, end-to-end discovery, human-AI interaction and intelligent interfaces, data-driven discovery, agents that can learn over time, methods for training agentic models, and the evaluation and benchmarking of agents.

Part of this work is conducted within a scientific domain rather than alongside one. We collaborate directly with research scientists at the Allen Institute and elsewhere on their primary data, including electrophysiology, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic measurements of human brain tissue. Our aim is to build agentic workflows that meet the standards of rigorous scientific work and to push the tools we already have to their full potential in support of research that is only now possible with AI. Doing this well depends on knowing when an  AI-generated hypothesis or causal claim is scientifically sound, and this calls for researchers who can evaluate such a claim against the underlying biology. We welcome applications from candidates trained in neuroscience or another life science who bring strong computational skills to that training.

We are seeking ambitious researchers with a background in biology or neuroscience, prepared to take on problems at the frontier of AI for science. You will be working on a neuroscience project, helping to find ways to use and advance asta tools to rapidly advance neuroscience research.

Topics you can explore during the internship:

  • Agentic planning, reasoning, learning, and evaluation.
  • AI workflows for scientific discovery.
  • Data-driven discovery (integrating your own or publicly available sequencing or electrophysiology dataset with AI workflows)
  • Evaluation of AI-generated hypotheses, causal claims, and analyses against experimental data and domain expertise.
  • AI workflows incorporating scientific literature and automated hypothesis generation and testing.

See our publications for examples of our work.

https://allenai.org/papers?tags=Asta
