We regularly publish in high-profile conferences in NLP (e.g., ACL, EMNLP), HCI (e.g., CHI, UIST, CSCW), ML (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR), IR (e.g., SIGIR), and Accessibility (ASSETS). A portion of this work is conducted jointly with domain scientists, on their datasets and their open research questions.

JOB SUMMARY:

As part of the Trace3xperience Program, the Security Intern will be offered an opportunity to integrate into Trace3's AI Security practice within Security Solutions. The practice helps enterprise clients adopt and scale AI securely, including AI models, applications, agents, data, and the pipelines and platforms they run on. The Tracer will be exposed to AI security assessment, strategy, architecture, and design engagements with a client base anchored in the Fortune 1000 space.

This internship is designed as a path into the Trace3 Service Delivery Organization. The objective is for the Tracer to become delivery-ready, meaning able to contribute to a client engagement under the supervision of more senior delivery consultants, by the end of the program. Internships typically run through the summer term and are frequently extended to three to four months, at which point Tracers who are delivery-ready are staffed on AI Security engagements within the Service Delivery Organization. 

Tracers in this program will receive accelerated professional development, exposure to all technical functions of an IT consulting organization, world-class mentoring, and unique networking opportunities across the organization.

 

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT TO LEARN:

Under the guidance of senior consultants and the Security leadership team, you will progress from structured learning and lab work, to shadowing and contributing on pre sales and delivery engagements, to owning defined work products yourself. Along the way you will learn:

  • How enterprise AI programs are built and where they break: the architecture of AI models, applications, agents, data, and the pipelines and platforms they run on, and how security applies at each layer.

  • How to apply AI security and Trustworthy AI frameworks and standards, including NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, OWASP Top 10 for LLM and Agentic Applications, MITRE ATLAS, and CSA AI controls, and how they connect to foundational cybersecurity frameworks such as NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and MITRE ATT&CK.
  • The AI platforms and native AI security capabilities of the major cloud service providers (AWS, Azure, GCP), and how clients actually deploy AI on them.
  • Emerging AI security problems, including trustworthy agents, agent-to-agent trust and delegation, non-human identity, and AI resilience, by contributing research and analysis to Trace3's point of view and solution plays.
  • How to translate technical AI security findings into business language for CISO-, CIO-, and executive-level audiences, and how to produce clear, well-structured client deliverables, documentation, and presentations.
  • How a technology consulting business works, including engagement scoping, statements of work, the handoff from Sales

description:
The Organization 

At USAFacts, we believe facts deserve to be heard. We turn data from thousands of jurisdictions into clear, unbiased answers about how government spends money and what it achieves. No political agenda. No commercial motive. Just public service.

Founded and funded by Steve Ballmer, former CEO of Microsoft, we work alongside Ballmer Group Philanthropy and Rainier Climate on civic impact.

As an intern, you’ll join a collaborative, mission-driven team and learn how complex public data becomes something the American people can actually use.

To top it off, Fast Company has recognized USAFacts four years running, including the 2026 Most Innovative Companies list. Learn more at usafacts.org and LinkedIn. Learn more about us at usafacts.org and linkedin.com/company/usafacts.

We’d love for you to bring your curiosity, and your conviction that facts matter, to your summer with us.

Your Internship with USAFacts

This is a paid, full-time summer internship, where you’ll do real work on real products. Here’s what to expect:

Pay

$30 per hour for at least 10 weeks, which comes to roughly $12,000 before taxes at 40 hours per week. Interns are overtime eligible, so hours over 40 per week are paid at time and a half.

Housing support

Relocating interns receive company-paid furnished corporate housing and a $1,000 travel reimbursement. Interns who live in the area and don’t need corporate housing can be reimbursed up to $2,000 per month for housing costs with a current rental agreement.

Paid sick days and holidays

3 paid sick days and paid holidays for the duration of your internship.

Hybrid schedule

In the office Tuesday through Thursday, with lunches provided, and the flexibility to work remotely or in-office the rest of the week.

Transportation

You’ll receive either an ORCA card for local public transit or paid parking in or near the building.

Events, community, and opportunities

At USAFacts, we believe a great internship is about more than just the work. Throughout the summer, you'll have opportunities to connect with your fellow interns, build relationships across the organization, and make the most of your time in the Seattle area. From organization-wide events and team outings to boat rides, paddleboarding adventures, and sushi dinners, you'll have plenty of opportunities to build connections and have fun along the way. Each intern cohort receives a dedicated morale budget to plan activities together and make the summer their own. You'll also have the unique opportunity to present your projects and accomplishments directly to USAFacts founder and former Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer and other organizational leaders.

The Opportunity

As a Content Team Intern at USAFacts, you’ll help turn complex government data into clear, engaging stories that people can trust. Working alongside our content team, you’ll help create, edit, and publish data-driven articles, social posts, infographics, and videos.

You’ll gain hands-on experience sourcing and cleaning data, building data visualizations, and interpreting what the numbers say for lay audiences, while learning how our team keeps content accurate, relevant, and unbiased.

This internship is a chance to build your data storytelling skills and portfolio and to work with a collaborative team dedicated to making reliable information about the country more accessible to everyone.

Key Priorities and Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with our brilliant team to create, edit, and publish engaging and data-driven content, including articles, blog posts, social media updates, infographics, videos, and other multimedia formats.
  • Source, clean, and analyze data sets to create data visualizations, and interpret the data to tell an unbiased story to lay audiences.
  • Conduct data analysis and research to uncover insights and trends that inform content development.
  • Routinely update and improve existing content to maintain relevancy, accuracy, and data-driven focus.
  • Monitor and analyze content performance metrics to identify trends, opportunities for improvement, and the overall impact of data-driven storytelling.
  • Adhere to deadlines and brand guides, ensuring timely publication and consistency in tone, style, and quality.
  • Stay informed of industry trends, best practices, and emerging content formats to ensure the content remains innovative and engaging.
  • Keep up on current events and social issues to identify both in-the-moment and evergreen content that will resonate with broad audiences.

The Ideal Candidate

  • Currently pursuing a quantitative-focused undergraduate degree in Data Science, Statistics, Economics, Public Policy, Public Administration, Political Science, Journalism or related
  • Currently in your Junior year of undergraduate study (graduating winter 2027 or spring 2028)
  • Data analysis: Experience with R, Python, SQL, or similar tools for data cleaning and analysis
  • Development workflow: Familiarity with Git, command line, NPM, and web development best practices.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication and storytelling skills, both verbal and written.
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.
  • Eagerness to learn and adapt in a dynamic work setting.
  • A genuine interest in product development and user experience.

description:
About Wheely

Wheely is redefining premium transportation across major cities in Europe, the US, and the Middle East. We blend cutting-edge technology with the craft of five-star chauffeuring to deliver an experience trusted by more than 100,000 active riders and 1,200 corporate accounts.

We’re a profitable, fast-growing scale-up with $43M raised and over $100M in annual revenue. Having recently launched in New York City, we’re expanding rapidly across the US and EMEA. If you take pride in your craft and want to help shape the next chapter of our growth, we'd love to hear from you.

Wheely runs a high-frequency, luxury marketplace — precision isn't a goal here, it's the baseline. As an Operations Intern in Paris, you'll work inside the France Operations team across the full chauffeur lifecycle: acquisition, retention, and day-to-day chauffeur management. This is a flexible internship (3 to 6 months, depending on your need) available immediately or in the coming weeks (starting no later than early January 2027).

This isn't a coffee-and-slides internship. You'll carry real workstreams, with real stakes, from week one.

Why This Role

  • High-growth business. Wheely France is scaling fast and expanding into new markets.

  • Turn data into clear, actionable insights — root-causing issues, tracking initiatives, and flagging what's working and what isn't.
  • Prepare data pulls, dashboards, and analyses for the wider Ops and leadership team.

Requirements

  • Clear communicator, able to summarise a complex point simply.
  • Available for 3 to 6 months.
  • Fluent French and English.
  • Based in Paris, ability to work full-time in the office 5 days a week.

What we Offer

  • Office-based role in Paris (9th arrondissement)

  • Monthly credit towards Wheely journeys

  • Real ownership on live projects, working directly with the France leadership team

All of your personal information will be collected stored and processed in accordance with Wheely’s Candidate Privacy Notice

description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

AI TUTOR, MEDICINE - TEMPORARY

In this role, you will help enhance Grok by creating and annotating high-quality data across the field of medicine. You will draw on your clinical expertise to evaluate model outputs, identify errors in clinical reasoning, and capture how clinicians think, communicate with patients, and navigate complex medical decisions. Your work will help train Grok to distinguish unsafe or clinically flawed responses from guidance that is evidence-based, diagnostically precise, and consistent with the standard of care. This work spans text, voice, and video, including recording audio and participating in video sessions.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Use proprietary software to create, label, and annotate data on defined medical projects.
  • Produce high-quality data efficiently, with exceptional attention to accuracy.
  • Help design and launch new medical data tasks, working closely with colleagues and technical staff to bring cutting-edge initiatives to life.
  • Partner with engineers to improve the design of fast, efficient annotation tools.
  • Help put trustworthy medical information within reach of patients and users worldwide.
  • Improve patient outcomes by solving real healthcare problems that train Grok to meet clinical standards across decision-making, drug discovery, diagnostic imaging, and procedures.
  • Create and solve complex medical problems within your area of expertise, such as diagnostic reasoning, treatment planning, care coordination, or image interpretation, writing detailed reference answers and critically evaluating model responses.
  • Interpret, analyze, and carry out tasks based on evolving instructions.

POSITION DETAILS:

This is a temporary position with SpaceXSI, for the length of time as stated, and is subject to change with minimal notice as business needs dictate.

  • LENGTH OF POSITION: 6 months (extensions or conversion to a permanent role may be available based on business needs).
  • LOCATION: Remote (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, India, and Australia); for US-based candidates, please note that we are unable to hire in Wyoming and Illinois at this time.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • MD, DO, MBBS, MBChB, DNP, PharmD, PsyD, DDS, DMD, DPT, DPM, OTD, or DVM degree, or an international equivalent of one of those degrees; OR a master’s degree or Ph.D. in nursing, physician assistant studies, clinical psychology, counseling psychology, public health, epidemiology, biostatistics, pharmacology, or biomedical sciences.
  • 2+ years of employment experience in a clinical, research, or health-related role after the qualifying degree was conferred (completion of a residency or other postgraduate training is not required; residency, fellowship, and internship positions count toward the experience requirement).
  • English proficiency at CEFR C1 level or higher.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Skill at navigating medical literature, databases, and online resources.
  • Excellent communication, interpersonal, analytical, and organizational skills.
  • Sound independent judgment when information is limited, and the ability to explain your reasoning clearly to others.
  • A genuine passion for innovation and for using technology to improve patient care.
  • Multiple publications, or a first-author publication, in a reputable journal or outlet.
  • Prior data annotation or teaching experience (as a professor, teacher, or tutor).
  • Experience in technical writing, medical writing, journalism, or another professional writing setting.
  • Post-graduate clinical experience or equivalent real world experience.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • This role may be offered as a full-time or part-time position depending on role/business needs and candidate availability; full-time positions are preferred and require working standard business hours in your local time zone.
  • We are unable to provide visa sponsorship.
  • Must be willing to travel to a SpaceXSI site.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

You’ll lead an independent research project exploring approaches to sim-to-sim and sim-to-real transfer for sensor-based driving models. Shape a real autonomy model: The tools and insights you create will help the team post-train our autonomy model more effectively, with the potential to influence the autonomy stack eventually deployed in Toyota vehicles. Collaborate with experienced researchers: Work closely with a small team of industry-leading researchers with deep experience in robotics and autonomous driving.
